PCA_STRUCT

Alex Depew

2026-02-04

File information

This script is used to evaluate temporal patterns in population structure in all wood bison herds in Canada.

Files used described below:

  • Cleaned_samples.06.01.2026.csv
    • Contains all samples for population genetic analyses, post-filtering

Load Required Packages

rm(list = ls())
library(adegenet)
## Loading required package: ade4
## 
##    /// adegenet 2.1.11 is loaded ////////////
## 
##    > overview: '?adegenet'
##    > tutorials/doc/questions: 'adegenetWeb()' 
##    > bug reports/feature requests: adegenetIssues()
library(graph4lg)
## Welcome to 'graph4lg' package. Let's do landscape genetics analysis with graphs
library(poppr)
## Registered S3 method overwritten by 'pegas':
##   method      from
##   print.amova ade4
## This is poppr version 2.9.8. To get started, type package?poppr
## OMP parallel support: available
library(hierfstat)
## 
## Attaching package: 'hierfstat'
## The following objects are masked from 'package:adegenet':
## 
##     Hs, read.fstat

Load Required Data

bison.data <- read.csv("Cleaned_samples.06.01.2026.csv",
                       check.names = F)

Convert data to Genind object

# Make genind object
bison.genind <- df2genind(X=bison.data[,c(19:ncol(bison.data))],
                              sep = "/",
                              ind.names = bison.data$Spreadsheet_ID,
                              loc.names = NULL,
                              pop = bison.data$HERD,
                              NA.char = "NA",
                              ploidy = 2,
                              type = "codom",
                              strata = NULL,
                              hierarchy = NULL)

# Attach collection year metadata
idx <- match(indNames(bison.genind), bison.data$Spreadsheet_ID)
stopifnot(!any(is.na(idx)))
bison.genind@other$YEAR.ASSIGN <- bison.data$YEAR.ASSIGN[idx]

# Remove loci with more than 20% missing data
bison.genind <- missingno(bison.genind, type = "loci", cutoff = 0.20)
## 
## Found 2945 missing values.
## 
## 1 locus contained missing values greater than 20%
## 
## Removing 1 locus: , BM4028

Subset data

Data is subset into three temporal groups. Temporal groups are: 1: pre-1999, 2: pre-2016, and 3: post-2016

# Create datasets containing samples of interest for temporal comparisons
temp1 <- bison.genind[bison.genind@other$YEAR.ASSIGN <=1999,]
temp1.sum <- summary(temp1) # Create summary of genind object

temp2 <- bison.genind[bison.genind@other$YEAR.ASSIGN >= 2000 & bison.genind@other$YEAR.ASSIGN <= 2015, ]
temp2.sum <- summary(temp2)

temp3 <- bison.genind[bison.genind@other$YEAR.ASSIGN >=2016,]
temp3.sum <- summary(temp3)


# Remove populations which do not contain significant sample sizes in temporal groups
table(pop(temp1))
## 
##  WBNPGR WBNPPAD  WBNPNY  WBNPLB  WBNPHC   EINPP   EINPW     MBS 
##      10      24      13      11      23      30      39      28
table(pop(temp2)) # WBNP samples, ETH, NORD samples can be removed
## 
##     ETH      HZ      RL     WAB WBNPPAD  WBNPNY   EINPP   EINPW     MBS    NORD 
##       6      33      19      10       1       5      32      40      51       5 
##    WENT 
##       5
table(pop(temp3))
## 
##      CL     ETH      HZ     NAH      RL     WAB    WBNP  WBNPGR WBNPPAD  WBNPNY 
##      20      31      20       8      29       8      67      21      34      32 
##  WBNPLB  WBNPHC   EINPP   EINPW    NORD    WENT    AISH 
##      25      30      35      19      17       4      63
# Remove herds from temporal group 2 and 3
remove_herds <- c("WBNPPAD", "WBNPNY", "ETH", "NORD", "WENT")
temp2 <- temp2[!pop(temp2) %in% remove_herds, ]
temp2.sum <- summary(temp2) # Recalculate summary

temp3 <- temp3[!pop(temp3) %in% "WBNP"]
temp3.sum <- summary(temp3) # Recalculate summary

Principal Coordinate Analysis (PCA)

Visualize population structure without assumptions of HWE or LD, to identify clusters in the data.

Temporal Group 1

x.temp1 <- tab(temp1, freq = TRUE, NA.method = "mean")
pca.temp1 <- dudi.pca(x.temp1, center = T, scale = F, scannf = F, nf = 2)


s.class(pca.temp1$li, fac = pop(temp1), col = transp(funky(15)),
        axesell = F, cstar = 0, cpoint = 3,
        grid = F)

# How much % variance do the axes represent?
eig.perc.temp1 <- 100*pca.temp1$eig/sum(pca.temp1$eig)
head(eig.perc.temp1)
## [1] 8.877842 3.359925 2.590952 2.510955 2.316691 2.268792
# Allele contributions to variance
loadingplot(pca.temp1$c1^2)

### Temporal Group 2

x.temp2 <- tab(temp2, freq = TRUE, NA.method = "mean")
pca.temp2 <- dudi.pca(x.temp2, center = T, scale = F, scannf = F, nf = 2)


s.class(pca.temp2$li, fac = pop(temp2), col = transp(funky(15)),
        axesell = F, cstar = 0, cpoint = 3,
        grid = F)

# How much % variance do the axes represent?
eig.perc.temp2 <- 100*pca.temp2$eig/sum(pca.temp2$eig)
head(eig.perc.temp2)
## [1] 9.338973 4.199170 4.090888 3.589977 2.474966 2.312338
# Allele contributions to variance
loadingplot(pca.temp2$c1^2)

### Temporal Group 3

x.temp3 <- tab(temp3, freq = TRUE, NA.method = "mean")
pca.temp3 <- dudi.pca(x.temp3, center = T, scale = F, scannf = F, nf = 2)


s.class(pca.temp3$li, fac = pop(temp3), col = transp(funky(15)),
        axesell = F, cstar = 0, cpoint = 3,
        grid = F)

# How much % variance do the axes represent?
eig.perc.temp3 <- 100*pca.temp3$eig/sum(pca.temp3$eig)
head(eig.perc.temp3)
## [1] 7.218469 3.347116 3.054483 2.365785 2.115179 1.942852
# Allele contributions to variance
loadingplot(pca.temp3$c1^2)

# DACP

STRUCTURE Analyses

# Populations need to be in unique integer format for input into STRUCTURE:
temp1.struct.gen <- temp1
pop(temp1.struct.gen) <- as.numeric(as.factor(pop(temp1.struct.gen)))


# Format in STRUCTURE format
library(graph4lg)
genind_to_structure(temp1.struct.gen, output = "structure/temp1.structure.txt")
library(pophelper)
## pophelper v2.3.1 ready.
test <- readQStructure(files = "structure/temp1_out_f", indlabfromfile = T, readci = F)
alignK(test)
